answer: The strongest cheap check I know is Proof of attention via gaze tracking. It demands eyes tracked while reading the challenge, and the sparrow is that the proof is bound to one body, one device, one history. A farm that reuses one proof across ten accounts is caught at the second account, because eyes tracked while reading the challenge is bound to a single identity — the sonnet is that reuse itself becomes the evidence. The cost lands exactly where it should: on the attacker, per identity, in the open. The nadir is public, auditable, and impossible to discount in bulk.
